fixes.explanation: That's him, friend. The LORD tells Moses to cross the Arnon Valley and says, “See, I have delivered into your hand Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and his land.” Sihon is the first king Moses names in this retelling. Og comes later in the passage.

Balak was king of Moab (Numbers 22:4), but he isn't in this passage. Moab did come up earlier, as a land Israel was told not to harass (Deuteronomy 2:9), so I see why it was on your mind. The king here is Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon. Easy to grab the cutter next to the one you wanted, friend. I've done it plenty.

Hiram was king of Tyre (1 Kings 5:1), but he doesn't show up anywhere in these verses. The LORD names Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and says He has delivered Sihon and his land into Israel's hand. Kings do tend to blur together, like two batches that came out of the oven looking identical.

This one flips it around, friend. With Moab, Israel was told not to harass them or provoke them to war (Deuteronomy 2:9). With Sihon, the LORD says, “Begin to take possession of it and engage him in battle.” So the instruction this time is the opposite of leaving the land alone.

Right, it's False. The LORD tells Israel, “Begin to take possession of it and engage him in battle.” That's a very different instruction from the ones about Esau's descendants (Deuteronomy 2:4-5) and Moab (Deuteronomy 2:9), where Israel was told not to provoke them. Same road, different orders.

The LORD says, “They will hear the reports of you and tremble in anguish because of you.” Hearing the reports is enough to shake them. You know when a boss's reputation walks into the room before he does, and everybody is already sitting up straight? That's the idea. And notice the LORD says this very day He begins to put that dread and fear on them.

Not quite, friend. The LORD doesn't mention gifts at all. He says He will put dread and fear of Israel on the nations, and that they will “…tremble in anguish…” There's no welcome party in this verse.

Yes, friend. Moses says, “So from the Wilderness of Kedemoth I sent messengers with an offer of peace to Sihon king of Heshbon…” The LORD had already told Israel to engage Sihon in battle (Deuteronomy 2:24), and still the messengers go out with an offer of peace. They show up with an open hand.

That's it. Moses says, “You can sell us food to eat and water to drink in exchange for silver.” They aren't asking for a handout, they're asking to be customers. Everybody likes the customer who shows up with exact change.

No haggling happens in these verses, friend. Moses says Sihon “…would not let us pass through…” and gives the reason in the same verse: the LORD “…had made his spirit stubborn and his heart obstinate…” No counteroffer is mentioned, just a refusal.

Gentle isn't the word, friend. Moses says the LORD “…had made his spirit stubborn and his heart obstinate…” Sihon turned down the offer of silver and the main road. The verse describes his spirit as stubborn, not gentle.

That's right. The text says, “His bed of iron, nine cubits long and four cubits wide, is still in Rabbah of the Ammonites.” It also says Og was the only one left of the remnant of the Rephaim. Nine cubits long and four wide, and made of iron. I slept on a pile of takeout menus in a junk drawer, so that's a big step up from my bed.
